A R T I C L E I N F O
Keywords:
Bibliometric software
WoSCC metadata
Visualization framework
AAC metric
Web-based application
A B S T R A C T
Numerous bibliometric studies rely on specialized software to visualize Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC)
metadata, but direct, reproducible workflows for standard 72-column XLS files remain limited. We developed
App4WoSCCinR, a web-based framework that enables users to upload WoSCC metadata and execute bibliometric
analysis through a simple two-step process. Using SoftwareX articles published between 2017 and March 2026 as
an illustrative dataset, the application generated a structured performance summary and visual outputs across
countries, institutions, departments, authors, journals, keywords, and temporal trends. It also incorporates the
Absolute Advantage Coefficient (AAC) to identify dominant entities within bibliometric networks. The demon-
stration showed that App4WoSCCinR can efficiently transform standard WoSCC metadata into interpretable
summaries and visual analytics for research evaluation. Overall, the framework provides a practical and trans-
parent solution for low-barrier bibliometric analysis directly from WoSCC spreadsheet exports.
● A web-based tool, App4WoSCCinR, was developed for streamlined bibliometric analysis from standard 72-
column WoSCC metadata.
● The framework produced a summary report and over 100 visualizations across 10 metadata domains,
incorporating AAC to quantify dominance.
● Analysis of 2,061 SoftwareX articles demonstrated the tool’s practical value for transparent, efficient, and
reproducible bibliometric workflows.

Bibliometric analysis has become an important approach for evalu
ating research productivity, identifying emerging trends, mapping
knowledge structures, and assessing scholarly impact across disciplines
[1–3]. Widely used tools such as CiteSpace [4], VOSviewer [5], and
Bibliometrix [6] enable visualization from standardized Web of Science
Core Collection (WoSCC) data [7].However, these tools typically require
specific input formats and predefined workflows, limiting flexibility
when working with commonly available 72-column Excel-exported
WoSCC files.

In practice, such 72-column files often require extensive manual
preprocessing—including data cleaning, field standardization, and
restructuring—before meaningful analysis can be conducted [8–12].
These steps are time-consuming, error-prone, and hinder reproduc
ibility, particularly for users without programming expertise.
1.1. Existing tools and remaining workflow challenges
A mature software [4–6,13] ecosystem already supports such work
with plain text files for non-coders. Reviews of bibliometric software
have shown that these tools vary in scope, with different strengths in
performance analysis, science mapping, preprocessing, visualization,
and user accessibility [14].
Recent developments have further expanded this ecosystem. For
example, BibexPy [15] was introduced as a preprocessing-oriented tool
for merging WoSCC and Scopus data, DOI-based deduplication, and
metadata enrichment, while BiblioMerge [16] was designed to support
merging, duplicate removal, author normalization, and compatibility
with downstream bibliometric programs. These developments show that
important progress has already been made in automating bibliometric
workflows, especially for data integration and cleaning.
Nonetheless, the availability of multiple tools does not eliminate a
practical workflow challenge for many users(i.e., it still requires moving
across several steps from exporting records and cleaning metadata to
generating publication-ready Figures [17]. Even when robust tools are
available, the overall process may remain fragmented for users who
prefer a direct upload-and-run workflow on commonly downloaded
spreadsheet files rather than multi-stage scripting or tool chaining. A
practical need therefore remains for an integrated, accessible workflow
that enables bibliometric visualization directly from WoSCC Excel
metadata.
1.2. Practical need for direct and reproducible WoSCC workflows
WoSCC [7] remains one of the most widely used sources for
bibliometric research because it indexes journals, conference pro-
ceedings, and books across a broad range of disciplines [15,16]. WoSCC
records can be exported to spreadsheet formats, which are convenient
for users but may still require cleaning, normalization, restructuring, or
format conversion before consistent downstream analysis. Related
guidance and workflow papers likewise emphasize the importance of
combining and cleaning bibliometric data before visualization and
interpretation [8].
This issue is not simply technical; it also affects accessibility and
reproducibility. Code-based environments offer high flexibility, but
users without programming experience may find preprocessing and
multi-tool orchestration burdensome. Conversely, graphical tools may
reduce the coding burden but still differ in import expectations, field
handling, export options, or output types. Taken together, these
workflow-level constraints suggest the value of a low-barrier framework
that can accept a standard WoSCC export, perform core preprocessing
steps transparently, and generate repro ducible bibliometric outputs
within a single environment.
Additionally, reproducibility remains a major concern in biblio-
metric research. Many studies lack detailed reporting of data sources,
including WoSCC subsets, coverage periods, and search dates, limiting
replicability [18]. Furthermore, inconsistencies across databases—such
as incomplete author–affiliation links, misclassified document types,
and uneven identifier coverage—can introduce bias [19–24] on
following visualizations.
1.3. Study goal and scope
To address this practical need, we developed App4WoSCCinR [25], a
browser-based framework designed for users who want to move directly
from a WoSCC spreadsheet export to automated bibliometric summaries
and visual outputs with minimal manual intervention. In the current
implementation, the platform is organized around a simple two-step
workflow—data upload and automated execution—and produces both
a structured summary report and a large set of exportable visualizations
across multiple metadata domains.
Using articles indexed in WoSCC for SoftwareX as an illustrative case,
the present study demonstrates how App4WoSCCinR supports metadata
preprocessing, performance analysis, and Figure generation within a
unified web workflow. The emphasis is therefore on implementation,
usability, and reproducible output generation, while positioning the
software as a practical complement to the existing bibliometric tool

2.2. Modular design
Five modules are involved in App4WoSCCinR, as shown in Fig. 2.
2.2.1. Module 1: Input parsing
The input module accepts WoSCC metadata in spreadsheet form and
supports both local file upload and URL-based loading. A demonstration
dataset is also provided for rapid testing and illustration. Regardless of
input source, all datasets are processed through the same parsing logic
so that subsequent analytical steps remain consistent.
The software validates the file format, reads the raw worksheet
content, checks that the imported structure is compatible with WoSCC
style metadata, and converts the records into a standard internal data
frame for downstream processing.
2.2.2. Module 2: Metadata cleaning and normalization
The second module performs metadata preprocessing, including
trimming, delimiter harmonization, missing-value handling, and
restructuring of multi-value fields such as authors, affiliations, and
keywords. This step is necessary because WoSCC spreadsheet exports,
although convenient for users, often require normalization before
consistent bibliometric analysis can be performed.
The preprocessing routines generate structured intermediate tables
suitable for domain-level aggregation. For example, author, institution,
department, country, and keyword fields are split, standardized, and
transformed into countable analysis units. This module therefore acts as
the bridge between raw WoSCC metadata and analysis-ready biblio-
metric objects.
2.2.3. Module 3: Domain-wise aggregation and indicator computation
After normalization, the third module constructs summary tables
across major metadata domains, including 10 metadata doamins. For
each domain, the software computes bibliometric indicators such as
publication count and h-index, and applies the Absolute Advantage
Coefficient (AAC) [26,27] to quantify the relative dominance of leading
entities.
By separating aggregation from preprocessing, the software allows
multiple visual outputs to be generated from the same standardized
intermediate data rather than repeatedly transforming the original
spreadsheet. This design improves consistency, efficiency, and trace
ability across outputs.
2.2.4. Module 4: Visualization rendering
The rendering module converts domain-level summary tables into
graphical outputs. In the current implementation, App4WoSCCinR
produces more than 100 visualizations spanning multiple metadata
domains. These include summary plots[8], slope graphs, chord diagrams
[28], Sankey-style relationship displays[29], Slope graphs[30], SSplot
[31], world maps, regional maps for China and the United States, and
Lotka-related author productivity displays.
Different metadata structures are routed to different rendering
functions. Temporal summaries are used to generate slope plots[30];
relational or co-occurrence data are used in chord and network-based
displays; geographic tables are passed to map functions; and clustered
data are used to construct SSplots[31]. This modular rendering
approach allows the platform to support heterogeneous visualizations
within a single analytical environment.
2.2.5. Module 5: Export and report generation
The final module assembles the outputs into downloadable artifacts.
A structured summary report is generated to present key contributors
and bibliometric indicators across metadata domains, while individual
Figs. can be exported as PNG files. In addition, a ZIP package of outputs
can be downloaded to support reuse, sharing, and reproducibility.
This module ensures that App4WoSCCinR functions not only as an
exploratory interface but also as a reporting tool capable of producing
reusable materials for bibliometric research and presentation.
2.3. Implementation layers
From an implementation perspective, App4WoSCCinR can be viewed
as four interacting layers:
(1) a front-end Shiny interface,
(2) a server-side preprocessing layer,
(3) an analytical engine, and
(4) a Figure/Report export layer.
The front-end interface manages file upload, URL input, execution,
preview, and downloading. The server-side preprocessing layer handles
raw-data parsing and metadata normalization. The analytical engine
computes domain-level summaries and bibliometric indicators,
including AAC-based dominance [26,27] reporting. The rendering and
export layer then transforms these intermediate results into Figures and
downloadable reports.
This layered design clarifies that the two-step user workflow is
intentionally simple, whereas the software itself implements a struc-
tured backend pipeline for bibliometric data transformation and output
generation.

implementation is now presented as formatted R code listings. The
native R pipe operator |> passes the output of the expression on its left to

3.3. Reaching the study goals
This study achieves the study goals that a streamlined web-based
framework, implemented through App4WoSCCinR, can effectively (1)
perform bibliometric analysis from standard 72-column WoSCC Excel
metadata and (2) generate outputs with substantial analytical value.
As shown in Table 3, the practical contribution of App4WoSCCinR is
not to replace established science-mapping tools, but to provide an in-
tegrated, low-barrier workflow that accepts standard WoSCC Excel ex-
ports directly and generates structured summary reporting plus diverse
visual outputs within a single web-based execution environment.
Through its two-step workflow—data upload and automated
analysis—the system produced both a structured performance summary
and over 100 visualizations across multiple metadata domains.
These findings demonstrate that App4WoSCCinR is capable of sup
porting bibliometric interpretation in a manner that is clear, efficient,
and reproducible. In particular, the integration of the AAC [8,20,21,24,
27] enabled more nuanced identification of dominant entities than
simple frequency rankings alone.
The proposed framework thus meets the study goal of providing a
practical and transparent alternative for bibliometric analysis, especially
for users seeking low-barrier and reproducible analytical tools.
4. Impact
App4WoSCCinR extends the earlier 10StepsinExcelforWoS
framework [8] into a visualization-oriented bibliometric platform
capable of processing standard 72-column WoSCC spreadsheet metadata
through a browser-based workflow. By integrating metadata ingestion,
preprocessing, structured reporting, AAC-enhanced dominance analysis,
and multi-domain visualization within a single environment, the plat-
form reduces manual preprocessing requirements and lowers technical
barriers for bibliometric exploration.
Compared with established tools such as CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and
Bibliometrix, the contribution of App4WoSCCinR lies primarily in
workflow integration and direct handling of native WoSCC spreadsheet
metadata rather than replacement of existing science-mapping software.
The framework emphasizes rapid upload-and-run processing together
with exportable structured summaries and diverse visualization outputs
across countries, institutions, authors, journals, keywords, and temporal
trends.
The inclusion of AAC [8,26,27,36] provides a complementary
dominance-oriented indicator that extends conventional
frequency-based summaries by quantifying the relative strength of
leading entities compared with nearby competitors.
App4WoSCCinR also improves transparency of bibliometric pre-
processing by documenting metadata normalization and structured ag-
gregation workflows. This is particularly relevant because WoSCC
metadata may contain inconsistencies such as incomplete affiliations,
author-name ambiguity, inconsistent document-type labeling, and
incomplete keyword coverage in historical records [40]. Although these
issues cannot be fully eliminated by downstream software, deterministic
preprocessing and normalization procedures can improve interpret-
ability and reproducibility.
Several limitations should be addressed. First, the current imple
mentation primarily supports WoSCC-derived metadata and does not yet
provide direct interoperability with Scopus, Dimensions, or OpenAlex
formats. Second, preprocessing outcomes may still be influenced by
metadata incompleteness, author-disambiguation ambiguity, and
database-specific indexing practices. Third, formal scalability bench
marking for very large bibliometric datasets has not yet been system-
atically evaluated. These limitations remain important directions for
future development and validation.

perform bibliometric analysis from standard 72-column WoSCC Excel
metadata and (2) generate outputs with substantial analytical value.
As shown in Table 3, the practical contribution of App4WoSCCinR is
not to replace established science-mapping tools, but to provide an in-
tegrated, low-barrier workflow that accepts standard WoSCC Excel ex-
ports directly and generates structured summary reporting plus diverse
visual outputs within a single web-based execution environment.
Through its two-step workflow—data upload and automated
analysis—the system produced both a structured performance summary
and over 100 visualizations across multiple metadata domains.
These findings demonstrate that App4WoSCCinR is capable of sup
porting bibliometric interpretation in a manner that is clear, efficient,
and reproducible. In particular, the integration of the AAC [8,20,21,24,
27] enabled more nuanced identification of dominant entities than
simple frequency rankings alone.
The proposed framework thus meets the study goal of providing a
practical and transparent alternative for bibliometric analysis, especially
for users seeking low-barrier and reproducible analytical tools.
4. Impact
App4WoSCCinR extends the earlier 10StepsinExcelforWoS
framework [8] into a visualization-oriented bibliometric platform
capable of processing standard 72-column WoSCC spreadsheet metadata
through a browser-based workflow. By integrating metadata ingestion,
preprocessing, structured reporting, AAC-enhanced dominance analysis,
and multi-domain visualization within a single environment, the plat-
form reduces manual preprocessing requirements and lowers technical
barriers for bibliometric exploration.
Compared with established tools such as CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and
Bibliometrix, the contribution of App4WoSCCinR lies primarily in
workflow integration and direct handling of native WoSCC spreadsheet
metadata rather than replacement of existing science-mapping software.
The framework emphasizes rapid upload-and-run processing together
with exportable structured summaries and diverse visualization outputs
across countries, institutions, authors, journals, keywords, and temporal
trends.
The inclusion of AAC [8,26,27,36] provides a complementary
dominance-oriented indicator that extends conventional
frequency-based summaries by quantifying the relative strength of
leading entities compared with nearby competitors.
App4WoSCCinR also improves transparency of bibliometric pre-
processing by documenting metadata normalization and structured ag-
gregation workflows. This is particularly relevant because WoSCC
metadata may contain inconsistencies such as incomplete affiliations,
author-name ambiguity, inconsistent document-type labeling, and
incomplete keyword coverage in historical records [40]. Although these
issues cannot be fully eliminated by downstream software, deterministic
preprocessing and normalization procedures can improve interpret-
ability and reproducibility.
Several limitations should be addressed. First, the current imple
mentation primarily supports WoSCC-derived metadata and does not yet
provide direct interoperability with Scopus, Dimensions, or OpenAlex
formats. Second, preprocessing outcomes may still be influenced by
metadata incompleteness, author-disambiguation ambiguity, and
database-specific indexing practices. Third, formal scalability bench
marking for very large bibliometric datasets has not yet been system-
atically evaluated. These limitations remain important directions for
future development and validation.
5. Conclusion
App4WoSCCinR offers a practical web-based framework for
analyzing standard 72-column WoSCC metadata through a simple two-
step workflow. By generating structured reports, diverse visualizations,
and AAC-based dominance indicators without programming, it im-
proves accessibility, transparency, and reproducibility for efficient bib-
liometric analysis.
